name: Shipping chokepoints
value: 3 ships hit 23 Nov; Iran vows tighter closure
summary: UKMTO reports three ships hit in Hormuz late on 23 Nov; Iran's army orders the strait closed further day by day
state: UKMTO said three eastbound vessels were struck by projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz late on 23 Nov and confirmed a fire after an attack on a ship anchored off the UAE; Iran's navy said two more tankers hit mines on 24 Nov (CBS News). Iran's army chief Amir Hatami ordered on 23 Nov that the strait be closed further day by day until Iran's conditions are met (Euronews). The JMIC recorded 114 US-assisted passages from 19 to 21 Nov and called Iran's mine claims unconfirmed. Hormuz traffic stays materially impeded.
for_you: Gulf energy and goods shipments face delays, rerouting and higher insurance costs, which feed through to fuel and freight prices. Anyone with travel or crew in the region should follow FCDO travel advice and UKMTO guidance.
rubric_hit: Alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded; ships struck 23 Nov and Iran orders a tighter closure

sources.title: Euronews — Iran orders Hormuz closed 'further day by day' as Qatar seeks to revive peace talks
CBS News — Iran war updates: ongoing attacks on tankers

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
